lessons.title: Seek First His Kingdom and His Righteousness
lessons.hear:
Whenever Xiaojie planned her schedule, she scheduled work first, then dates, and last of all her quiet time, “when I have time.” But by the time she had a free moment, she was already so tired that all she wanted to do was scroll on her phone. She said, “It’s not that I don’t love God. I just don’t have time.”

Jesus said, “But seek first God’s Kingdom and his righteousness; and all these things will be given to you as well.” (Matt 6:33) The word “first” speaks of order, not of length of time. You may give God only ten minutes a day, but if you put it first, it will change the other twenty-three hours and fifty minutes.

This is not a trade. It does not mean that seeking God first will get you the person or the thing you want. It is an invitation: put God’s Kingdom at the center, and God will take care of our needs and renew our desires. When the order is right, time does not become a battlefield.
lessons.light: Jesus is my example: he sought his Father’s Kingdom first, and even his eating and sleeping were within the Father’s arrangement. The Bible is my standard: seek first his Kingdom and his righteousness. The Holy Spirit is my guide: he reminds me of the order and supplies what I need. Those who live in selflessness put God first and let Jesus be King.
think: According to Matt 6:33, what are we to seek first?
Where is God’s place in my schedule?
How can I make “seeking his Kingdom first” the first thing of every day?
lessons.speak: Heavenly Father, thank you for knowing everything I need. Help me seek your Kingdom and your righteousness first, and not put you last. Give the first part of each day to you, and help me trust that you will take care of the rest. Amen.
lessons.do: Tomorrow when you wake up, before you look at your phone, spend five minutes reading a verse and praying. Today, move your phone farther from your alarm clock, or set a reminder.
lessons.quick: When the order is right, time does not become a battlefield.
text: But seek first God’s Kingdom and his righteousness; and all these things will be given to you as well.

lessons.title: Only One Thing Is Needed
lessons.hear:
Xin was very capable in ministry and took care of everything: sound, hospitality, fellowship meals. But one day she said to a friend, “I haven’t sat quietly before God for a long time, and I haven’t really listened to my friends either.”

Martha received Jesus into her home and was busy preparing many things, but Mary sat at the Lord’s feet and listened. Martha was upset, and Jesus answered, “but one thing is needed. Mary has chosen the good part, which will not be taken away from her.” (Luke 10:42)

Jesus did not blame Martha for serving. He said gently that she was anxious and troubled about many things. Serving, dating, and working are all good things, but if they push out my closeness with the Lord, we lose what is essential. The only thing that is needed is to sit at his feet. This one thing will not be taken away, and it becomes the strength of all my relationships.
lessons.light: Jesus is my example: he accepted Martha, and he also invited her to sit down. The Bible is my standard: only one thing is needed. The Holy Spirit is my guide: even in the busyness, he lets me still hear the Lord’s gentle voice. Those who live for self prove their worth by what they do; those who live in selflessness first sit at the Lord’s feet and are loved.
think: According to Luke 10:42, which good part will not be taken away?
Am I more like Martha or Mary right now? What keeps me busy?
Today, how can I sit at the Lord’s feet first, even in the middle of being busy?
lessons.speak: Lord Jesus, I am often like Martha, anxious and troubled about many things. Let me sit at your feet, listen to your word, and receive your love. In my serving, my dating, and my work, let everything begin from you and return to you. Amen.
lessons.do: Today find a fifteen-minute block, turn off your notifications, and read just one passage from a Gospel, quietly listening to God. When you finish, write one sentence: What did you say to me today?
lessons.quick: Only one thing is needed: to sit at the Lord’s feet.
text: As they went on their way, he entered into a certain village, and a certain woman named Martha received him into her house.
She had a sister called Mary, who also sat at Jesus’ feet and heard his word.
But Martha was distracted with much serving, and she came up to him, and said, “Lord, don’t you care that my sister left me to serve alone? Ask her therefore to help me.”
Jesus answered her, “Martha, Martha, you are anxious and troubled about many things,
but one thing is needed. Mary has chosen the good part, which will not be taken away from her.”

lessons.title: Come Away and Rest
lessons.hear:
Looking back on this week: redeeming the time (Eph 5:15–16), counting our days (Ps 90:12), seeking his Kingdom first (Matt 6:33), the one thing that is needed (Luke 10:42).

When Jesus’ disciples came back from ministry, so many people were coming and going that they did not even have time to eat. Jesus said to them, “Come away into a deserted place, and rest awhile.” (Mark 6:31) Rest is not laziness; it is the Lord’s invitation.

Some people in a relationship always want “a little more time” together; some people who are single fill their emptiness with busyness. Either way, the Lord is saying: Come, rest awhile. Resting is admitting that I am not God, and that the world will not collapse if I take a day off.

This week, is there a place where you need to stop?
lessons.light: This week’s 3-2-1: Jesus is my example, and he took his disciples away to rest; the Bible is my standard, seek God’s Kingdom first and God will take care of the rest; the Holy Spirit is my guide, giving me order and rest in my time. Those who live for self treat themselves as a god who cannot stop; those who live in selflessness let God be God, and let themselves be human.
think: Where did I see self this week? How did God support me in it?
In Mark 6:31, what does Jesus invite the disciples to do?
What one thing will I delete or postpone next week so that I can truly rest?
lessons.speak: Heavenly Father, thank you for inviting me to rest awhile. Forgive me where I have been unwilling to stop and have wanted to prove myself through busyness. Let me find rest in you, and let me spend my time on what matters most. All the glory be to you. Amen.
lessons.do: Today set aside at least one hour to do nothing for the sake of efficiency: take a walk, take a nap, or sit in silence. Afterward write in your journal: while I was resting, what did God say to me?
lessons.quick: Rest is the Lord’s invitation, not a betrayal of efficiency.
text: He said to them, “Come away into a deserted place, and rest awhile.” For there were many coming and going, and they had no leisure so much as to eat.

weeks.keyText: Therefore watch carefully how you walk, not as unwise, but as wise, redeeming the time, because the days are evil.

weeks.title: Money and Daily Life
weeks.theme: Money is a servant, not a master; put it back in the servant’s place, and love will not be bought and sold.
group: Read Matt 6:24. Which two masters does Jesus say we cannot serve at the same time? What does this look like in life today?
In your heart, is money more like security, achievement, control, or a tool?
What one honest and specific adjustment do you want to make with money this week? Ask your group members to pray for you.
weeks.sunday: After the Sunday gathering, find a trusted partner and say, “The place where I most need God in my finances is…” and pray for each other. When you get home, write down the biggest non-essential expense this month and give it to God.
weeks.weekend: This weekend do a “money review”: list this month’s income, fixed expenses, giving, savings, and entertainment. Then share your review with a trusted friend or an older mentor and ask him to give you one reminder. You don’t need to have a partner, and you don’t need to disclose the numbers; just be honest.

lessons.title: You Can’t Serve Both God and Mammon
lessons.hear:
Han put great weight on a partner’s “qualifications”: salary, job stability, whether the family owns a home. He said this was not being materialistic but being responsible. But whenever he talked about the future, what was on his mind was how to make himself feel secure, not how to serve God together, and that made even him feel something was off.

Jesus said, “No one can serve two masters, for either he will hate the one and love the other, or else he will be devoted to one and despise the other. You can’t serve both God and Mammon.” (Matt 6:24) Mammon is money treated as a master.

Money itself is not sin, and being short of money is nothing to be ashamed of. The question is whether it is a servant or a master. When a person makes money the source of security, he will use it in relationships to measure, to compare, and even to control. Jesus asks us to choose one master, because the heart can have only one king.
lessons.light: Jesus is my example: he had nowhere to lay his head, yet he never lacked, because he depended on the Father. The Bible is my standard: you can’t serve both God and Mammon. The Holy Spirit is my guide: he helps me recognize the other master in my heart. Those who live for self use money to protect themselves; those who live in selflessness let God be my provider.
think: According to Matt 6:24, which would a person choose between two masters?
Does my heart depend more on God, or on the security money brings?
As I look for a relationship, do I put too much weight on the other person’s finances?
lessons.speak: Lord, help me recognize where in my heart money has taken a place. Forgive me for putting my security in money. Let me serve you alone, and in my relationships let me value a person’s life more than their qualifications. Amen.
lessons.do: Today take five minutes to write: “If I didn’t have this money, what would I have left?” Then, in one sentence, give this worry to God.
lessons.quick: Money is a servant, not a master; the heart can have only one king.
text: “No one can serve two masters, for either he will hate the one and love the other, or else he will be devoted to one and despise the other. You can’t serve both God and Mammon.

lessons.title: Godliness With Contentment Is Great Gain
lessons.hear:
Xin’s boyfriend often wanted to buy a new phone or a new car. He said, “This is to give you a better life.” Xin felt uneasy, because she did not feel she needed these things, but she was afraid that saying so would make her look unambitious. So she said nothing and just worried quietly.

Paul says, “But godliness with contentment is great gain. For we brought nothing into the world, and we certainly can’t carry anything out. But having food and clothing, we will be content with that.” (1 Tim 6:6–8) Contentment is not a lack of effort; it is understanding what is enough.

In dating, a content person does not use material things to prove love, and does not use them to measure love. They are willing to live a simple life together, and they can also be generous together. We do not need to compare the size of gifts or the places we go on dates, because what truly lasts is godliness and a contented heart.
lessons.light: Jesus is my example: he taught us to pray, “Give us today our daily bread.” The Bible is my standard: godliness with contentment is great gain. The Holy Spirit is my guide: he gives me the peace of having enough. Those who live for self always feel it is not enough; those who live in selflessness already have enough in Christ.
think: According to 1 Tim 6:6–8, what is great gain?
Do I measure love, or get measured, by money and gifts in a relationship?
What are three things I already have that I can thank God for today?
lessons.speak: God, thank you for providing my daily bread and clothing. Give me a contented heart, so that I do not compare myself with others and do not use material things to prove love. Make me simple and generous in my relationships, and give me the peace of having enough. Amen.
lessons.do: Today write down five things that are “already enough” for you, at least two of which are not material. Before you sleep, read this list aloud to God.
lessons.quick: Contentment is not a lack of effort; it is knowing what is enough.
text: But godliness with contentment is great gain.
For we brought nothing into the world, and we certainly can’t carry anything out.
But having food and clothing, we will be content with that.

lessons.title: First Sit Down and Count the Cost
lessons.hear:
Xiang and his girlfriend planned a trip. Both wanted to go somewhere more expensive, and they ended up using several months of savings and even putting it on a credit card. After they came back, they argued over the repayments, the relationship was strained for a while, and even the meetings they had looked forward to felt heavy.

Jesus said, “For which of you, desiring to build a tower, doesn’t first sit down and count the cost, to see if he has enough to complete it?” (Luke 14:28) Counting the cost is wisdom, not stinginess. In dating, if two people have not sat down beforehand to talk about spending, borrowing, and shared expenses, these often turn into pressure on the relationship.

Remember also: before marriage, do not lend large sums of money to the other person, and do not co-sign any debt for him. If the other person asks you to hand over all your accounts, controls your income, or uses money to threaten you, that is not love but control, and you need to seek help from trusted people and professional organizations.
lessons.light: Jesus is my example: he taught us to count the cost before we act, not to go on a moment’s enthusiasm. The Bible is my standard: first sit down and count the cost. The Holy Spirit is my guide: he helps me stop before I act on impulse, and helps me be honest about money. Those who live for self spend by feeling; those who live in selflessness keep their stewardship before God.
think: According to Luke 14:28, what must be done before building a tower?
Have I ever spent or borrowed beyond my means because of a relationship or friends?
How can I honestly talk about money principles with someone important to me?
lessons.speak: Lord, give me wisdom, so that before I spend money I sit down and count the cost. Keep me from being carried away by a moment’s enthusiasm, and give me the courage to say no. May I be a faithful steward of what you have entrusted to me, and help me face my own limits honestly. Amen.
lessons.do: Today list “the three biggest expenses this month,” and write down which of them was necessary. If there is any borrowing or a shared account, first consult someone you trust.
lessons.quick: Counting the cost is wisdom, not stinginess.
text: For which of you, desiring to build a tower, doesn’t first sit down and count the cost, to see if he has enough to complete it?

lessons.title: A Cheerful Giver
lessons.hear:
An gave every month on schedule, but she often felt a heaviness in her heart, as if she were paying taxes, always quietly counting how much was left. Once, while chatting with a friend, she realized she had been giving reluctantly because she was afraid of being seen, not because she was truly glad to.

Paul says, “Let each man give according as he has determined in his heart, not grudgingly or under compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver.” (2 Cor 9:7) Gladness comes from seeing that God gave us everything first. We give, not to buy blessings, and not to show ourselves off, but to respond to grace.

Generosity in relationships is the same. Toward friends, toward the person you are dating, toward those in need, giving comes from the abundance in the heart, not to trade for love and not to hold on to the relationship. True generosity does not leave a debt, and does not make the other person feel indebted.
lessons.light: Jesus is my example: for our sake he became poor, so that through his poverty we might become rich. The Bible is my standard: God loves a cheerful giver. The Holy Spirit is my guide: he lets us give from gratitude, not from pressure. Those who live for self give to get something back; those who live in selflessness give in response to grace.
think: According to 2 Cor 9:7, what kind of giving does God love?
When I give, am I cheerful, reluctant, or wanting to be seen?
Today, how can I gladly give something to someone in need?
lessons.speak: Heavenly Father, thank you for giving me everything first. Cleanse my motives for giving, so that I do not give to be seen or to trade for love, but give out of gratitude. Teach me to be cheerful, and let my hands be a channel for your blessing to others. Amen.
lessons.do: Today do one small act of generosity: buy someone a drink, give some of your time, or give quietly. Don’t tell anyone; tell only God.
lessons.quick: God loves a cheerful giver, one who gives not to be seen but to respond to grace.
text: Let each man give according as he has determined in his heart, not grudgingly or under compulsion, for God loves a cheerful giver.

lessons.title: In Any and All Circumstances, the Secret
lessons.hear:
Looking back on this week: you can’t serve two masters (Matt 6:24), a contented heart (1 Tim 6:6–8), counting the cost (Luke 14:28), a cheerful giver (2 Cor 9:7).

Paul says, “I know how to be humbled, and I also know how to abound. In any and all circumstances I have learned the secret both to be filled and to be hungry, both to abound and to be in need. I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me.” (Phil 4:12–13) This secret is not a technique; it is depending on Christ.

Some people feel empty in abundance, and some have peace in lack. If this week you found yourself anxious about money, comparing, or suffering from financial pressure in a relationship, don’t be discouraged. This can be learned, and Paul “learned” it too.

If you are facing pressure from debt or financial control, please also reach out to people you trust and to professional organizations, and don’t carry it alone.
lessons.light: This week’s 3-2-1: Jesus is my example, and he depended on the Father in both abundance and lack; the Bible is my standard, a contented heart is great gain; the Holy Spirit is my guide, helping me learn the secret in every circumstance. Those who live for self let money be king; those who live in selflessness let Jesus be King, and all the glory goes to God.
think: Where did I see self this week? How did God support me in it?
In Phil 4:13, what kind of strength does “all things” refer to?
What one money habit will I adjust next week?
lessons.speak: Lord Jesus, thank you for being the provider of my life. Forgive me where I have been anxious, comparing, or controlling because of money. Teach me to depend on you in both abundance and lack, so that I am not bound by money in either. All the glory be to you. Amen.
lessons.do: In your journal write: my biggest discovery about money this week; one habit I will adjust; one person I need as a reminder. Today send that person a message inviting him to walk with you.
lessons.quick: In Christ, whether in abundance or in lack, I have learned the secret.
text: Not that I speak because of lack, for I have learned in whatever state I am, to be content in it.
I know how to be humbled, and I also know how to abound. In any and all circumstances I have learned the secret both to be filled and to be hungry, both to abound and to be in need.
I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me.

weeks.title: With God, With Friends, With the Community
weeks.theme: Love is not two people hiding away; love grows healthy among God, friends, and the community.
group: Read Prov 27:17. Is there an “iron sharpens iron” friend in your life? How does he help you become sharper?
Do your current relationships bring you closer to God, friends, and the community, or are they slowly drawing you out?
Which friend or older mentor do you want to reach out to this week for a deeper conversation? Ask your group members to pray for you.
weeks.sunday: After the Sunday gathering, find someone who usually doesn’t say much, reach out to him with a word of care, and agree to have a phone call this week. Then say to a partner: “One thing I am willing to let you remind me about is…”
weeks.weekend: Plan a gathering of three or more people this weekend: a meal, a walk, or serving together, with the theme “greeting one another.” Each person shares one thing they are thankful for this week and one thing they need prayer for, and everyone prays for him together. You don’t need to have a partner; those who are single or dating can both come.

lessons.title: Iron Sharpens Iron
lessons.hear:
After Yu got a girlfriend, he slowly drifted out of small group and rarely had meals with his old friends. He said, “Having each other is enough in our world.” Three months later, when he and his girlfriend had a conflict, he found that he had no one around him to talk to.

Proverbs says, “Iron sharpens iron,” and in the same way a person sharpens his friend. (Prov 27:17) When iron rubs against iron, there is friction and there are sparks, and it makes each one sharper. A true friend does not say only pleasant things, but also reminds me gently and honestly.

Dating is not two people hiding away together, but two people growing together in God’s household. A person with friends has someone to celebrate with when the relationship is going well, and someone to walk with when it is hard. You need friends like that, and you can be that kind of friend to others.
lessons.light: Jesus is my example: he chose twelve disciples to walk with him, and he also had three who were closest to him. The Bible is my standard: friends sharpen one another. The Holy Spirit is my guide: he places us in a community where we sharpen one another. Those who live for self only want to be praised; those who live in selflessness are willing to be reminded and sharpened.
think: According to Prov 27:17, what is the relationship between friends like?
In my circle of friends, is there anyone who dares to tell me the truth? Whom do I dare to tell the truth to?
Whom can I invite today to be my “iron”?
lessons.speak: Lord, thank you for giving me friends. Give me one or two people who are willing to remind me honestly, and make me willing to accept their reminders. Keep me from leaving the community because of a relationship, and let me instead be shaped within the community into what pleases you. Amen.
lessons.do: Today send a message to a friend you haven’t been in touch with for a long time and say: I’ve been thinking of you, and I’d love to hear how you’ve been. Set a time to meet or talk.
lessons.quick: A true friend makes me sharper and brings me closer to God.
text: Iron sharpens iron; so a man sharpens his friend’s countenance.

lessons.title: Do Not Forsake Assembling Together
lessons.hear:
After Ying started dating, she often used “Sundays are for dates” as a reason to miss Sunday gatherings. Once she said to a friend, “I know it’s not good, but every time I say I want to go, he gets upset, and I don’t want to argue.”

Hebrews says, “Let’s consider how to provoke one another to love and good works, not forsaking our own assembling together, as the custom of some is, but exhorting one another, and so much the more as you see the Day approaching.” (Heb 10:24–25) Gathering is not an obligation; it is the place where we support one another.

If a relationship gradually leads you away from God’s household and away from your friends, stop and take a look. A truly good relationship will bring you back to God’s household, not pull you away. If the other person uses emotions, threats, or the silent treatment to keep you from gatherings or from seeing friends, this is a red flag of isolation, and you need to seek help from a trusted pastor and friends.
lessons.light: Jesus is my example: it was his custom to go into the synagogue on the Sabbath. The Bible is my standard: do not forsake assembling together, and provoke one another to love. The Holy Spirit is my guide: he weaves us into one body that belongs to one another. Those who live for self make the relationship everything; those who live in selflessness love people in God’s household.
think: According to Heb 10:24–25, what is the purpose of gathering?
Have I cut back on gatherings and fellowship because of a relationship or being busy?
Today, how can I return to a regular fellowship?
lessons.speak: Heavenly Father, thank you for placing me in your household. Keep me from leaving my brothers and sisters because of any relationship, and in our gatherings teach me to look out for one another. Give me courage to keep my appointment with you, even in a relationship. Amen.
lessons.do: Today confirm the time of the next Sunday gathering and small group, put them in your calendar, and tell the people involved ahead of time: this time is reserved for God.
lessons.quick: A good relationship will bring you back to God’s household, not pull you away.
text: Let’s consider how to provoke one another to love and good works,
not forsaking our own assembling together, as the custom of some is, but exhorting one another, and so much the more as you see the Day approaching.

lessons.title: With Many Counselors, There Is Safety
lessons.hear:
Kai was deciding whether to start dating a girl he had not known long. He struggled inside, yet he asked only himself and did not dare ask anyone else, because he was afraid people would say he was moving too fast or being too impulsive. Later he found that he had ignored many warning signs, and only when someone asked did he realize he had never said out loud the unease in his heart.

Proverbs says, “Where there is no wise guidance, the nation falls,” but with many counselors there is safety. (Prov 11:14) A counselor is someone who is willing to tell you the truth and who knows the Bible. In dating, we are most easily blinded by emotion, and at such times an onlooker often sees more clearly.

Seeking counselors is not handing the decision over to someone else; it is to see your own blind spots. The final decision is still between you and God. A good counselor asks questions, prays, and points you to the Bible, and does not decide for you.
lessons.light: Jesus is my example: before major decisions he went up the mountain to pray first, and he also walked with his disciples. The Bible is my standard: with many counselors there is safety. The Holy Spirit is my guide: he often reminds me through other people’s mouths. Those who live for self make their own decisions; those who live in selflessness are willing to be reminded and willing to seek companions.
think: According to Prov 11:14, why do we need counselors?
When I make major relationship decisions, whom do I usually ask?
Which mature brother or sister can I invite today to be my counselor?
lessons.speak: Lord, give me people who are willing to tell me the truth and who love you, to be my counselors. Make me humble, willing to hear my own blind spots, and let my final decision come from your leading and not from my feelings of the moment. Amen.
lessons.do: Today list two mature brothers or sisters as your “counselor list.” Choose one and send a message: I’d like to ask you to pray for something in my life and give me some reminders.
lessons.quick: Counselors help me see my blind spots; the final decision is still before God.
text: Where there is no wise guidance, the nation falls, but in the multitude of counselors there is victory.

lessons.title: Rejoice With Those Who Rejoice
lessons.hear:
Xiaowen’s friend had just gotten engaged. She typed congratulations in the group chat, but inside she felt sour. She said to herself, “Am I terrible? Someone else is happy, and I’m not.”

Paul says, “Rejoice with those who rejoice. Weep with those who weep.” (Rom 12:15) This verse does not ask us to suppress our feelings; it invites us to see others and enter into their situation. Rejoicing with others takes humility, and weeping with others takes courage.

We often look at other people’s joy through comparison, and use busyness to avoid other people’s tears. But Jesus went to the feast with those who rejoiced, and he also wept with those who wept. When we can rejoice and weep with others, our hearts are set free from our own lack. At the same time, we can honestly tell God about our bitterness, and he will not blame us.
lessons.light: Jesus is my example: he rejoiced at the wedding in Cana, and he wept at Lazarus’s tomb. The Bible is my standard: rejoice with those who rejoice, and weep with those who weep. The Holy Spirit is my guide: he softens my heart to enter into other people’s situations. Those who live for self compare; those who live in selflessness are present.
think: According to Rom 12:15, how are we to treat other people’s joy and weeping?
When a friend has good news, what do I truly feel inside?
Today, what is one concrete thing I can do for a friend’s joy or sorrow?
lessons.speak: Lord Jesus, thank you for being willing to rejoice with those who rejoice and weep with those who weep. Heal the bitterness and comparison in my heart, so that I can sincerely be glad for others and keep company with those who grieve. Make my heart soft like yours. Amen.
lessons.do: Today send sincere congratulations for a friend’s good news, or sit for a while with someone who is weeping, giving no advice, just keeping them company.
lessons.quick: Rejoicing and weeping with others is the freedom of being released from comparison.
text: Rejoice with those who rejoice. Weep with those who weep.

lessons.title: I Have Called You Friends
lessons.hear:
Looking back on this week: iron sharpens iron (Prov 27:17), do not forsake assembling together (Heb 10:24–25), many counselors (Prov 11:14), rejoicing and weeping with others (Rom 12:15).

Jesus said, “No longer do I call you servants, for the servant doesn’t know what his lord does. But I have called you friends, for everything that I heard from my Father, I have made known to you.” (John 15:15) Jesus is not only our Lord; he also calls us friends. He tells us what is on his heart, and he walks with us.

This is the most secure friendship, and it is the starting point of every relationship. When I know that I am someone Jesus calls a friend, I do not need to prove myself through other people’s acceptance, and I do not need to hide in a relationship to escape loneliness.

This week, did you notice where you have been avoiding community? Which friend do you need to reconnect with?
lessons.light: This week’s 3-2-1: Jesus is my example, and he calls us friends; the Bible is my standard, do not forsake assembling together; the Holy Spirit is my guide, joining us into one body. Those who live for self hide in a relationship; those who live in selflessness walk with others in God’s household. Let Jesus be King, and the glory goes to God.
think: Where did I see self this week? How did God support me in it?
According to John 15:15, why does Jesus call us friends?
Which friend will I reconnect with next week?
lessons.speak: Lord Jesus, thank you for calling me a friend. Forgive me where I have hidden in a relationship and drawn away from the community, and make me willing to return to your household and walk with my brothers and sisters. Make me a friend to others as well. All the glory be to you. Amen.
lessons.do: In your journal write: where I most need my friends’ support this week; one person I will reconnect with; whose friend I am willing to be. Send him a message today.
lessons.quick: Jesus calls me a friend, so I don’t need to hide in any relationship.
text: No longer do I call you servants, for the servant doesn’t know what his lord does. But I have called you friends, for everything that I heard from my Father, I have made known to you.

weeks.keyText: Iron sharpens iron; so a man sharpens his friend’s countenance.
